issues.item: Threat: Irritability: Irritable behavior, angry outbursts, or acting aggressively
issues.explanation: 'Irritability' is not a threat appraisal/perception item; it reflects arousal/behavioral dysregulation and fits better outside the Threat node. In this profile, the other Threat items are coherent terrorism-related hypervigilance/safety behaviors ('Scanning Exits', 'Back to Wall'), so this item is internally mismatched within the node and weakly aligned with the formulation in which Memory-linked threat should reflect perceived current danger rather than aggressive behavior.

vignette: Tunde is a 33-year-old African American man who has been struggling with symptoms following a traumatic event involving terrorism. Tunde works as a tailor and lives alone in an apartment near his shop in a bustling urban area. The trauma he experienced occurred about six months ago when a terrorist attack struck the city during a public festival. On that day, Tunde had gone to the festival after receiving a consignment of fabric for his tailoring business. The event was vibrant with music and dancing until an explosion shattered the atmosphere. In the chaos that followed, Tunde found himself caught in a panic-stricken crowd. He recalls bits and pieces but has memory gaps for critical moments during the attack. What he can remember is like a film playing over and over in his mind-images of people screaming, debris flying, and a pervasive sense of danger. Since then, Tunde's life has been dramatically altered by his trauma. His tailoring shop, once a sanctuary filled with vibrant fabrics and patterns, now feels more like a place where he can hide from the world outside. He avoids going out as much as possible, spending long hours on his phone playing games or browsing the internet to avoid thinking about what happened. This habit has begun to affect his work; deadlines are slipping, and orders have been delayed because Tunde often loses track of time. When he does venture out, Tunde's hypervigilance is palpable. He scans for exits as soon as he enters any room or building, ensuring that his back is always against a wall so he can see the entire space. This constant scanning and positioning leaves him feeling exhausted and on edge all the time. At times, he feels completely numb when recalling the event, as if it happened to someone else rather than himself. Tunde's self-doubt has grown over time, exacerbated by his feelings of not belonging anywhere. He no longer trusts that he will do the right thing in a crisis and often wonders why he survived while others did not. This sense of weakness is overwhelming; he feels vulnerable and exposed, as if any moment could bring another attack. In an attempt to cope with these overwhelming emotions, Tunde sometimes seeks conflict or creates drama. He picks arguments with clients over minor issues, convinced that the attention will distract him from his trauma. These confrontations have strained relationships at work and led to several conflicts with suppliers, making it harder for him to maintain a stable business. Despite his efforts to avoid future plans, he has found himself increasingly isolated. Friends and family members have noticed his withdrawal and attempts to engage him in activities or outings are met with resistance. Tunde feels that planning anything might set him up for another disaster. This constant fear of what could happen next has made it difficult for him to connect with others on a meaningful level. It was the culmination of these issues-struggling at work, feeling isolated, and constantly living in fear-that finally brought Tunde to seek help. He is most afraid that he will never feel safe again, that every moment holds potential danger. Yet, there is also hope; he is hoping for some relief from his symptoms and a way to reclaim control over his life without feeling like he's walking on eggshells all the time. Through therapy, Tunde hopes to regain trust in himself and find ways to engage with the world again without being constantly overwhelmed by fear. He wants to feel like he belongs somewhere and to reconnect with the sense of purpose he once had as a tailor, no longer overshadowed by his trauma.
